phase1_assignment: verify every proposed dependency-elimination route against exact primary-source scope, artifact, and claim boundaries before it may support elimination
candidate_context: A stale role-local continuation named SkillEvo. This invocation re-evaluated that candidate under the current Phase-1 dependency-elimination assignment rather than inheriting the stale conclusion.
tested_claim: Whether the current primary-source evidence for SkillEvo is sufficient to support elimination of any Phase-1 platform, capability, quota, Work, or manual-human dependency class.

primary_source.title: SkillEvo: Self-Renewing Evolution Gradients from Multi-Turn Interaction Feedback

verified_scope.evaluation_design: Tickets are chronologically split per Skill; the first three quarters drive evolution and the fourth quarter is held out solely for evaluation. Reported TSR is measured on the held-out evaluation set.
verified_scope.mechanism_boundary: Failures are attributed to Knowledge Gap, Capability Limit, or Evaluation Noise; only Knowledge Gap enters the Skill revision loop. Permission/tooling restrictions, delivery problems, infrastructure faults, and evaluation noise are explicitly excluded from Skill repair.

verified_claims: The paper reports improvements in the tested cloud-support Skill-evolution setting and states deployment in Tencent Cloud production.
The framework uses a held-out evaluation quarter that is not fed back into the evolution loop.
The framework explicitly separates Skill-repairable knowledge gaps from capability limits such as permission/tooling restrictions and infrastructure faults.
An independent governance layer is used to detect and repair factual and structural degradation of revised Skills.

verdict_reasoning: The primary evidence is scoped to evolution of textual Skills for cloud technical support; it does not establish removal of platform, execution-surface, paid/quota, Work, or human-authority dependencies.

The paper itself classifies permission/tooling restrictions and infrastructure faults as Capability Limit rather than Skill-repairable Knowledge Gap, which directly prevents treating SkillEvo as evidence that those dependency classes are eliminated.
Production deployment supports operational relevance within the reported Tencent Cloud setting, but does not broaden the tested authority or dependency boundary beyond that setting.
Therefore SkillEvo may inform a bounded skill-maintenance mechanism, but it cannot be counted as Phase-1 dependency-elimination evidence for the protected dependency classes.

may_support: bounded mechanisms for multi-turn feedback-driven textual Skill maintenance
held-out evaluation discipline within the tested setting
separation of knowledge-gap repair from capability-limit failures
must_not_support: elimination of Work or protected-primary execution dependency
elimination of finite quota or paid-model dependency
elimination of platform or tooling capability dependency
elimination of manual or account-holder authority
general production-safety or AGI claims outside the paper's tested scope
